content:
Anika: TL;DR — sketch for packing credits + microqueue topology to untangle admission from batching. Short notes before RFC update.
Devon: ok
Anika: admission issues: current headroom is leaky under bursts. Idea: admission mints numeric packing credits (units ~= output tokens). Batcher spends credits to assemble a GPU batch; refunds on eviction.
Ravi: credit conservation is critical. We need idempotent refunds and a fast ledger (atomic counters).
Marta: ops want per-tenant microqueues so noisy neighbors don't starve others. Prefer microqueues feeding a central coalescer with weighted RR.
Devon: tradeoffs: microqueues increase scheduler CPU (O(#hot tenants)) but give isolation. Shared queue is simpler but fairness is hard. We can cap microqueues to hot set via LFU.
Anika: affinity token idea: admission returns small affinity id; batcher biases co-location but treats it as soft preference. TTL on tokens to avoid staleness.
Ravi: fallback mode: if admission RPC times out, batcher uses local conservative heuristics and emits ADMISSION_FALLBACK events.
Marta: observability: track credits_in, credits_spent, refunds, fallback_count, p99_batch_latency. Alert if refund_rate > 5% for 5m.
Devon: impl notes: lock-free ring for hot path, CAS ledger for credits, cheap refund path.
Anika: tests: credit conservation, eviction/refund races, perf at 50k rps with 1k hot tenants. Action: I'll draft wire schema; Devon prototype ring; Ravi bench harness; Marta ops/runbook.
Anika: final: will update RFC with invariants and failure modes.
